method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis' (last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed), 40 claims; LICENCE: © The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne; Terms clause 5.2, personal use only; paraphrased and hash-anchored (read at https://www.rch.org.au/ (Terms and Conditions, clause 5.2)). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne 'RCH flowcharts for Bronchiolitis' (management approach diagram on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1), 12 claims; LICENCE: © The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne; Terms clause 5.2, personal use only; paraphrased and hash-anchored (read at https://www.rch.org.au/ (Terms and Conditions, clause 5.2)). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 rebuilds the hand-written Wave 1 page (which quoted RCH) as a paraphrase. Every Wave 1 claim is carried over and re-anchored in the page as fetched on 2026-09-24. S2 anchors point into a text transcription of the management diagram made in Wave 1; the diagram itself is an image and was not re-read.

claims.claim: **Diagnose it clinically;** tests are not needed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Aim of care:** keep the infant oxygenated and hydrated. Apart from simple pain relief, no medicine is indicated.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ex-premature infants and those with heart or lung disease** deteriorate more often and are more likely to be admitted.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Nasal prong oxygen when SpO2 stays below 90%;** keep high-flow nasal prong (HFNP) therapy for when standard nasal prong oxygen has failed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **What it is:** a viral infection of the lower respiratory tract, usually in infants below 12 months, diagnosed from the typical history and examination.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Course:** worst at about day 2-3 after the work of breathing increases, settling over 7-10 days (the course varies). It resolves on its own and usually needs no treatment; the cough can last weeks.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Onset:** a runny-nose prodrome, then any of cough · fever · feeding difficulty · apnoeas · irritability or unsettledness.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Risk factors for more serious illness:** congenital heart disease · chronic lung disease · chronic neurological conditions · born before 37 weeks, or under 10 weeks old at presentation · growth restriction · Indigenous ethnicity · immunodeficiency · cigarette smoke exposure · trisomy 21.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Consider admitting infants with these risk factors** even when they present early with mild symptoms.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **On examination:** fast breathing · accessory muscle use · wheeze and/or fine crackles on both sides · hypoxia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Most infants need no tests.** Investigate only if the child deteriorates or the diagnosis is in doubt (for example a murmur with signs of heart failure).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **No chest X-ray:** it cannot tell viral from bacterial infection, is poorly reproducible at this age, and can prompt needless antibiotics.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **No blood tests** (not a gas, full blood examination or blood culture).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **No viral swab or aspirate** for managing the individual child; the result should not steer treatment.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Treatment is supportive:** adequate oxygen, adequate fluids, and handling the infant as little as possible.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Observation without treatment:** some young infants with risk factors, or with apnoeas (no breath for more than 15 seconds, often with a slow heart rate and/or desaturation), benefit from a stay in hospital even if they need neither fluids nor oxygen.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Target SpO2: 90%,** unless an underlying heart or lung condition sets its own target.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Short, mild or moderate dips below 90% are expected** and are not a reason to start oxygen.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Start nasal prong oxygen only for SpO2 that stays below 90%.** If it stays below 90% and 2 hours of low-flow oxygen have not improved breathing, move to HFNP.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **No HFNP** for an infant whose SpO2 is consistently 90% or more.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Wean oxygen down to the least that keeps SpO2 at 90% or more;** there is no need to push saturations into the mid or high 90s.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Every 6 hours, try the infant off oxygen, whether HFNP or nasal prong;** restart nasal prong oxygen if SpO2 is still under 90%.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Off oxygen for 2 hours → stop saturation monitoring.** Keep observations 2-4 hourly, and bring back intermittent oximetry if the infant worsens.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Keep offering comfort oral feeds;** infants tend to settle better. If other hydration is needed, use a nasogastric (NG) tube first; it is safe during respiratory support.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **NG bolus feeds are safe;** start at two-thirds of maintenance because ADH secretion may be raised.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **IV fluids only when NG feeding is not possible;** use an isotonic fluid with glucose added.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Simple analgesia only;** other medicines are not routinely indicated.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Chloral hydrate** can settle agitation in an infant whose respiratory distress is worsening, whether or not they are on respiratory support; it works best under 2 years and under 15 kg.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Chloral hydrate dose, 0-2 years:** start at 10 mg/kg every 4-6 hours; if needed go to 15 mg/kg, then up to 20 mg/kg every 4-6 hours. ⚠️ Outside critical care, closer monitoring and senior involvement are required.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Chloral hydrate adverse effects:** oversedation · respiratory depression · hypotension · paradoxical agitation. Take care in renal or hepatic impairment.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Caffeine:** not enough evidence to use it to prevent apnoea in bronchiolitis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not give:** beta-2 agonists (even with personal or family atopy) · corticosteroids by any route (nebulised, oral, IM or IV) · adrenaline by any route (nebulised, IM or IV) unless the infant is peri-arrest or in arrest · nebulised hypertonic saline · antibiotics, azithromycin included · antivirals · caffeine.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Nasal suction:** not deep (beyond the nasopharynx). Superficial suction may help a moderately affected infant feed; saline nose drops at feed times may be considered.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **No chest physiotherapy.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Two assessments side by side:** breathing (respiratory status) and hydration.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Bronchiolitis', management approach diagram on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchilitis.jpg, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Not persistently hypoxaemic (SpO2 90% or more in air):** discharge, unless moderate to severe work of breathing, risk factors for severe disease or apnoeas justify a period of observation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Bronchiolitis', management approach diagram on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchilitis.jpg, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Persistently hypoxaemic:** low-flow nasal prong oxygen at 2 L/min; hourly observations in moderate disease, continuous if severely unwell. ⚠️ Severe or life-threatening illness: get an ICU review and start HFNP or CPAP.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Bronchiolitis', management approach diagram on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchilitis.jpg, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Review the response within 2-3 hours,** sooner if the infant is unwell.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Bronchiolitis', management approach diagram on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchilitis.jpg, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Still hypoxaemic (below 90%), tachycardic, tachypnoeic or working hard after 2-3 hours?** If the hypoxaemia is only mild and the infant is otherwise better, a longer trial of nasal prong oxygen is an option.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Bronchiolitis', management approach diagram on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchilitis.jpg, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Improving:** titrate and wean oxygen to keep SpO2 at 90% or more; stop saturation monitoring once off oxygen for 2 hours or more.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Bronchiolitis', management approach diagram on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchilitis.jpg, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Not improving:** consider HFNP at 2 L/kg per min, adjusting FiO2 to keep SpO2 at 90% or more.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Bronchiolitis', management approach diagram on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchilitis.jpg, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Response to HFNP means:** SpO2 90% or more · better heart rate, breathing rate and/or work of breathing · no significant or repeated apnoeas with desaturation or bradycardia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Bronchiolitis', management approach diagram on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchilitis.jpg, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **No response to HFNP:** get paediatric intensive care advice (on site or through retrieval); consider CPAP in severe disease.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Bronchiolitis', management approach diagram on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchilitis.jpg, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Responding to HFNP:** wean FiO2 towards room air keeping SpO2 at 90% or more; try off oxygen every 6 hours, restarting nasal prong oxygen if SpO2 is under 90%; stop HFNP once stable in air.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Bronchiolitis', management approach diagram on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchilitis.jpg, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Hydration branch:** if intake is below 50% over 12 hours or the infant is clinically dehydrated, start NG feeds at 2/3 of maintenance, and stop them once 2/3 of feeds are taken by mouth.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Bronchiolitis', management approach diagram on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchilitis.jpg, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Observation regardless of treatment:** with apnoeas, moderate to severe work of breathing or risk factors for severe disease, consider keeping the infant in hospital even if no oxygen or fluids are needed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Bronchiolitis', management approach diagram on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchilitis.jpg, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Talk to the local paediatric team** if the infant has a listed risk factor · needs oxygen · is taking under half the usual feeds and is clinically dehydrated · has moderate or severe respiratory status.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Think about transfer** for severe bronchiolitis · risk factors for severe illness · care beyond what the local hospital is comfortable with · HFNP needing FiO2 above 50%.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Discharge** once SpO2 is 90% or more and feeding is adequate. ⚠️ Infants under 8 weeks are more likely to re-present.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Hospital in the Home on home oxygen** may suit selected infants after observation, per local policy. Explain the illness to parents, how it is expected to progress, and when and where to get help.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Currency:** PIC endorsed; page last updated November 2023.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Key evidence cited:** Dalziel et al., Lancet 2022, and the 2018 Australasian Bronchiolitis Guideline from the PREDICT network.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Bronchiolitis', last updated November 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Bronchiolitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24
